drafted_from: tool:keep-the-shared-checkout-current's own row (its words, input schema, wake and steps) and the procedure in its README; read it before relying on it
start_here: Nothing to say: the engine runs tool:keep-the-shared-checkout-current every 5 minutes on the Mac that holds the shared Workshop checkout. To read its last pass, say to your AI: "Show the last pass that kept the shared Workshop checkout current." It answers {"outcome":"ran","behind_before":12,"behind_after":0,"rescue_ref":"refs/rescue/workshop-shared-20261120-003000","kept":[],"trashed":[],"skipped":[]}.
no_lists_because: It keeps no row: it reads and moves files in one granted checkout and answers what it did.
instructions: 1. Leave it on: the wake every-five-minutes runs the tool at the Mac that holds the checkout, with the checkout as its granted change-a-folder folder.
2. Read each pass: outcome ran means the checkout is at origin/main when behind_after is 0; refused or stopped means nothing in the working tree was written, and why says what held it.
3. Look at kept first: each path there is someone's work that the pass left in place, with why. Commit or move it yourself; the next pass does not touch it.
4. Find a saved state under refs/rescue/workshop-shared-<time>: it is local only and never pushed; delete it only after its contents are safe elsewhere.

worked_examples.title: Read the last pass
worked_examples.ask: Show the last pass that kept the shared Workshop checkout current.
worked_examples.given: An empty input: the tool reads its granted checkout, not the input.
worked_examples.hands_back: A JSON pass result such as {"outcome":"ran","behind_before":12,"behind_after":0,"kept":[{"path":"tools/example/x.mjs","why":"changed here"}],"trashed":[],"skipped":[]}, where every kept or skipped path carries its why.
